# Comparison: Two Reading-Intervention Programs for Grade 3

## Overview

This comparison weighs Program R against Program L for a Grade 3 reading intervention. Program R follows a structured phonics sequence. Program L uses guided reading with leveled texts. The evidence base favors structured phonics for early decoding gains [1]. Guided reading shows stronger results for fluency practice once decoding is secure [2]. Cost and training demands differ sharply between the two.

## Comparison Matrix

| Criterion | Program R | Program L |
|---|---|---|
| Decoding gains | Strong, replicated [1] | Modest |
| Fluency gains | Modest | Strong after decoding secure [2] |
| Teacher training | 3 days intensive | 1 day introduction |
| Materials cost per class | High first year | Moderate, recurring |
| Fit for struggling readers | Strong | Mixed |

## Detailed Analysis

Program R delivers its largest gains in the first intervention term. Two randomized evaluations report effect sizes above 0.4 for decoding measures [1]. The program demands sustained fidelity to its sequence. Deviations reduce its measured advantage.

Program L works best as a follow-on rather than a starting point. Classes that entered with secure decoding showed fluency gains [2]. Classes that entered without decoding showed stalled progress. The program's flexibility suits confident teachers with stable groups [3].

Costs diverge over three years. Program R concentrates spend in year one for materials and training. Program L spreads smaller recurring costs across license renewals [3]. A hybrid sequence captures both programs' strengths: structured phonics first, then guided reading for fluency.

## Recommendation

Adopt Program R for the first two terms. Transition struggling readers into Program L groups once decoding checks pass. Revisit the split at each term boundary using the running records.

## Bibliography
[1] Author, D. (2023). Structured phonics sequences in early intervention. Reading Research Annual.
[2] Author, E. (2024). Guided reading after decoding mastery. Literacy Studies Journal.
[3] Author, F. (2022). Cost profiles of commercial reading programs. Education Economics Notes.
